# Foreword

This operating model is for conducting are exploratory, didactic analyses and is not intended to inform management decision making at this stage. All data used in the construction of these operating models are publicly available from sources that are cited. 

<br>
<hr>


# Introduction

This operating model aims to closely mimic a [recent stock assessment for South African Sardine by de Moor (2025)](https://science.uct.ac.za/maram/2025-workshop) for the purposes of testing the robustness of management procedures to projected climate changes originating from an Ecoystem Model (Ortega et al. XXX). 

The assessment includes a recently revised hypothesis for sardine stock structure and includes West and South stock components with varying somatic growth ([Assessment Document BG4, de Moor 2025](https://science.uct.ac.za/sites/default/files/media/documents/science_uct_ac_za/2066/iws-2025-sardine-bg4.pdf)). 

The focus of this operating model is capturing the overall stock dynamics in terms of resilience, magnitude and natural variability for the purpose of evaluating under projections, various management porcedures (MP) that set annual advice. As such the focus not capturing the detailed historical spatial and seasonal dynamics necessary to interpret historical data correctly (a primary challenge for the assessment) but rather to use the assessment estimates for evaluating MPs. For this reason the operating model is spatially aggregated and captures the stock-wide dynamics informed by the recent stock assessment. 

<br>
<hr>

# Methods

## OpenMSE 2.0

OpenMSE operating models were configured to match the aggregate age-structured dynamics of the [stock assessment](https://science.uct.ac.za/sites/default/files/media/documents/science_uct_ac_za/2066/iws-2025-sardine-bg4.pdf) closely matching the estimates of harvest rate, recruitment and biomass. 

## OM Initialization 

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
library(openMSE)
library(readxl)
packageVersion('MSEtool') # should be v4x

# AI extracted estimates of recent assessed biomass, recruitment, harvest rate, selectivity, maturity and somatic growth
est_yr =  as.data.frame(readxl::read_xlsx('Data/SA_Sardine_2025_estimates.xlsx', 'ByYear'))
est_len = as.data.frame(readxl::read_xlsx('Data/SA_Sardine_2025_estimates.xlsx', 'ByLength'))
est_age = as.data.frame(readxl::read_xlsx('Data/SA_Sardine_2025_estimates.xlsx', 'ByAge'))

# Create blank operating model and fill details
om = new('om') 
om@Name = "South African Sardine"
om@Longitude = 20
om@Latitude  = -35
om@Author = 'Tom Carruthers'
om@Agency = 'Blue Matter'
om@Email = 'tom@bluematterscience.com'
om@Region = "South Africa"
om@Sponsor = "The Ocean Foundation"
om@Source = "https://climatetest.bluematterscience.com"

# Basic Config
Years = est_yr$Year           # historical year labels
ny = length(Years)            # number of historical years
om@nYear = ny                 # historical year
om@pYear = 50                 # 50 projected years
om@Interval = 1               # management updated every 1 year
om@DataLag = 1                # data available from last year (not in-season management)
om@nSim = 48                  # No. realisations of stock and fleet dynamics
om@CurrentYear = max(Years)   # label for most recent historical year
om@Years = Years(om)          # all year labels
om@Seasons = 1                # Annual OM
om@maxF = 3                   # maximum apical exploitation rate is 3.0 (harvest rate of 95%)
om@Seed = 1                   # random seed for stochastic sampling
om@Log[[1]] = paste("OM created:", Sys.Date()) 

```

## Stock and Fleet Initialization 

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
stock = new('stock')
stock@Name = 'South African Sardine'
stock@CommonName = 'Sardine'
stock@Species = 'Engraulis encrausicolus'

fleet = new('fleet')
fleet@Name = "All commercial fleets (inc directed sardine and round herring)"
```


## Natural mortality rate 

The operating model assumes the same natural mortality as the recent stock assessment (following the 2022 assessment of [de Moor (2022)](https://doi.org/10.25375/uct.22146602.v1)) that is 1.0 per year for juveniles (age 0) and 0.8 for mature fish (age 1+). 

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
stock@Ages = Ages(6, MinAge = 0)                                            # Age 6 is the last age class for calculations of age-based vectors
stock@NaturalMortality = NaturalMortality(MeanAtAge = c(1.0, rep(0.8,6)))   
plot(stock@Ages@Classes,stock@NaturalMortality@MeanAtAge, pch=19, lwd=2, xlab = "Age", ylim = c(0,1), ylab = "Inst. Nat. M. (per year)"); grid()
```

## Somatic Growth

Combined South + West from 2025 assessment [de Moor 2025](https://science.uct.ac.za/sites/default/files/media/documents/science_uct_ac_za/2066/iws-2025-sardine-bg4.pdf).

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
Classes = 1:ceiling(max(est_age$Length)*1.3)   
stock@Length = Length(MeanAtAge = c(est_age$Length,est_age$Length[6]),  # Need to add another asympotic length to make 7 age classes (first is age-0)
                      Classes = 1:ceiling(max(est_age$Length)*1.3) )    # Length classes
plot(0:6,stock@Length@MeanAtAge, lwd=2, type="l",xlab = "Age", ylab = "Length (cm)"); grid()
```

## Maturity

The maturity ogive was specified according to the MSE operating model ogive identified by [de Moor (2025)](https://science.uct.ac.za/sites/default/files/media/documents/science_uct_ac_za/2066/iws-2025-sardine-bg5.pdf). This prescribes a logistic model with a length 50% maturity of 11.8811 cm with a rate of increase in maturity at length of 1.9311

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
stock@Maturity = Maturity(MeanAtLength = 1/(1+exp(-(Classes - 11.88)/1.93)))
plot(Classes,stock@Maturity@MeanAtLength, lwd=2, type="l",xlab = "Length (cm)", ylab = "Fraction Mature"); grid()
```

## Recruitment

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}

B = est_yr$B_west + est_yr$B_south # Biomass Mt (could be unitless, R0 and steepness h are the targets)
R = est_yr$R_west + est_yr$R_south # Billions of fish

BH<-function(par, B, R, mode='opt', plot = F, tplot = F, curyr = 2024, pmu = 0.6, pcv = 0.1){ # optimization function for Bev-Holt SR
  h = 0.2 + 0.8 * (1 / (1 + exp(par[1]))); R0 = exp(par[2]);  BpR = max(B,na.rm=T) / R0       # logit between 0.2 and 1
  Rpred<-((0.8 * R0 * h * B) / (0.2 * BpR * R0 * (1 - h) + (h - 0.2) * B))                    # predicted recruitment 
  if(plot) {plot(B,R,pch=19); points(B, Rpred,col='red');                                     # plot fitted SR curve 
            legend('topleft',legend=c(paste("h =",round(h,3)),paste("R0 =",round(R0,3))),text.col="red",bty="n")}
  if(mode=='opt')return(-sum(dnorm(log(Rpred)-log(R),0,0.5,log=T), na.rm=T)-dnorm(pmu,h,pcv,log=T))  # add prior on h
  if(mode != "opt") return(log(R / Rpred))                                                    # return log rec devs
}

opt = optim(par = c(0,log(max(R,na.rm=T)/2)), BH, # optimize for h and R0 from initial values of 0.6 and half the max R
            B =  B, R = R, method = "L-BFGS-B",   # bounded optimization
            lower = c(-4,log(10)),                # broad limits
            upper = c(4,log(50)))                 # broad limits


RD = BH(opt$par, B, R, plot=T, mode = "devs") # recruitment deviations  
R0 = exp(opt$par[2])                          # 'unfished' recruitment
h = 0.2 + 0.8 * (1 / (1 + exp(opt$par[1])))   # steepness of the B-H S-R function
AC = acf(RD[!is.na(RD)],1)$acf[2,1,1]         # lag-1 recruitment autocorrelation
SD = sd(RD, na.rm=T)                          # lognormal recruitment process error ('sigma-R')          


DepGuess = (B[1]/mean(B,na.rm=T))                                           # depletion guess
RecDevInit = matrix(DepGuess, nrow = om@nSim, ncol = stock@Ages@MaxAge+1)   # initial rec devs (year 1)
RecDevHist = matrix(RD,nrow = om@nSim, ncol = ny, byrow = T)                # historical rec devs
RecDevProj = matrix(NA,nrow = om@nSim, ncol = om@pYear)                     # projected rec devs
nterminal = sum(is.na(RD))                                                  # No. terminal years in need of filling
fyears = rev(rev(om@Years)[1:(nterminal + om@pYear)])                       # labels for years that need filling
res = MSEtool::GenResiduals(SD, AC, fyears, om@nSim, TruncSD = 3)           # generated residuals with AC and SD
RecDevHist[,(ny-nterminal+1):ny] = res[,1:nterminal]                        # populate terminal rec devs
RecDevProj = res[, (nterminal+1):ncol(res)]                                 # populate projected rec devs

stock@SRR = SRR(Pars=list(h=h), R0 = R0, AC = AC, RecDevInit = RecDevInit,  # build Stock Rec. Rel. slot
                RecDevHist = RecDevHist, RecDevProj = RecDevProj)

matplot(Years(om, Period = "P"), t(RecDevProj[1:4,]),lty=1,type="l",
        xlab="Proj. Year",ylab ="Rec. Dev.", main="4 Simulations"); grid()
legend('topleft',legend=c(paste("SD =",round(SD,2)),paste("Lag-1 AC =", round(AC,2))))

```

## Selectivity 

Commercial fishery selectivity follows the length-vector of the most recent estimated year of the stock assessment.

## Scale optimization

Two components of the OM specification need to be adjusted to match estimated biomass, recruitment and harvest rate: unfished recruitment (scale), apical F mismatch. 

To do this we initialize the OM, estimate harvest rate, biomass and recruitment and wrap this into a bivariate optimization for unfished recruitement and apical F modifiers.

# Software

## OpenMSE


The [openMSE R package](https://openmse.com) was used to organize fishery data, define operating models, condition operating models to data, calculate reference points and specify and test existing and alternative management options. 

Visit the [OpenMSE website](https://openmse.com) for more information on the framework including tutorial and case studies.

The Rapid Conditioning Model is also [described there](https://openmse.com/tutorial-rcm)

Other useful openMSE apps include [MERA](https://www.merafish.org/) for rapidly scoping operating models and [Reference Point Calculator](https://shiny.bluematterscience.com/app/rpc) for investigating reference points and control rules. 

## Management Strategy Evaluation

The Ocean Foundation host the [Harvest Strategies website](https://harveststrategies.org/) which is an excellent resource describing MSE, MSE concepts and how MSE can be used in fishery management including introductory videos and interviews with experts. 'Harvest strategy' and Management Procedure are synonymous by the way.
